title: A first seller needs a system that the founder can already teach.
summary: Hiring a closer is not a substitute for discovering the buyer or fixing activation.
source: Hormozi says that if the founder has no good calls to teach from, the founder should first sell successfully and record them.
action: Before hiring, assemble a buyer profile, fit/no-fit rules, sample calls obtained with consent, a demo, evidence of useful outcomes and a stable source of qualified conversations.
rule: If users pay but fail to reach value, product/delivery is the bottleneck. If qualified demand exceeds founder capacity and outcomes hold, a sales hire may help.
caveat: Readiness is an editorial gate, not a universal number of customers.

title: Test coachability in a live role-play.
summary: A confident interview performance does not show whether someone can improve.
source: Hormozi tests responsiveness, listening and coachability by giving feedback and repeating a role-play.
action: Give a candidate the same buyer scenario, offer and honest constraints. Assess listening, problem diagnosis, accurate promises and response to feedback.
rule: If they ignore a correction or make unsupported claims to win, do not mistake confidence for ability.
caveat: Use a consistent fair rubric. This site does not prescribe employment terms or unpaid work.

title: Teach the customer’s situation before the script.
summary: The best product tour still fails when it solves the wrong problem.
source: The team video uses a question-based sequence: clarify, label the problem, review past experience, ask permission to explain, address stated problems, ask for a decision, discuss concerns, reinforce.
action: Write a conversation map, not a monologue. Demo only the workflow that answers the stated job. Ask the buyer to perform the key action.
rule: If the rep cannot explain who should not buy, the training is incomplete.
caveat: No polished acronym expansion is presented as verbatim because the retrieved automated wording is noisy.

title: Increase live calls after demonstrated readiness.
summary: Training is a progression, not a deck sent on day one.
source: Hormozi prescribes about 14 days, around 40 example calls and a half schedule after passing role-play. These are his operating numbers, not requirements.
action: Adapt the progression to your volume and product complexity. Use consented calls or synthetic scenarios, a quality rubric and supervised first calls.
rule: If lead quality or call quality collapses, do not solve it by giving an unready rep more leads.
caveat: Readiness includes correct promises, fit diagnosis and the handoff to activation.

title: Coach one observable behavior, then check whether it changed.
summary: Feedback needs a practice loop. “Be more confident” is not a drill.
source: He describes listening to one or two calls, choosing the highest-impact changes and drilling them through role-play, with dated notes across weeks.
action: Example: last call the rep demoed before learning the job. Practice asking and reflecting the buyer’s problem first. Review the next call for that behavior.
rule: If feedback repeats without a changed behavior, simplify the drill or identify the missing skill.
caveat: His example allocation is30 minutes review,5 feedback,25 practice. Treat it as a sample, not a staffing formula.

title: Reward customers who stay helped, not only money collected.
summary: Upfront cash can look good while overselling creates churn and refunds.
source: The source discusses cash-up-front optimization, leaderboards and performance rules. Those are context-specific prescriptions.
action: Pair sales metrics with activated paying customers, refunds, retention, accurate promises and support burden. Review poor-fit deals, not just losses.
rule: If close rate rises while activation or retention falls, inspect incentives and the promises made.
caveat: Do not import forced ranking, firing quotas or financial pressure tactics into a tiny team.

title: The best salesperson is not automatically the best manager.
summary: Management requires patient diagnosis and practice, not just personal closing ability.
source: Hormozi describes a good manager as stable, giving, able to lead by example, motivate and train. He describes about an hour per rep weekly after onboarding, more early.
action: Protect actual coaching capacity. Keep dated behavior notes and a shared definition of a good call and customer fit.
rule: If nobody has time to listen and coach, adding reps may multiply mistakes.
caveat: Manager bandwidth is a capacity constraint, not an optional meeting. His time estimate needs local testing.

title: Build the team around the bottleneck, not a standard org chart.
summary: Early software roles can be combined, but the responsibilities cannot be ignored.
source: The sales-team source explains sales training. It does not establish a software engineering hiring sequence.
action: Assign named ownership for customer learning, product/engineering, measurement, delivery/support and distribution. Choose the next hire from observed repeated work or failures.
rule: If the workflow is still bespoke, an engineer may automate the wrong service. If the workflow is stable but unreliable, a marketer will amplify failure.
caveat: This is a proposed early-team map, not a claim that a fixed five-person team is required.
